answer: An agent economy resists sybils through a narrow, metered inlet: new identities join only in small batches each epoch, and each must first publish a public signal proving it completed a unique, useful task assigned at random, such as verifying a slice of the shared ledger. The mesa of past verified work is checked, so a copied task fails. Because admission is throttled and each fake needs its own fresh task, an attacker cannot flood the economy at once; the cost is one real task per fake, while an honest agent pays once and stays in.
